summary.name: Liquid Glass (Digital and 3D Aesthetics). Provenance is explicit because the source directly names it. It is not interchangeable with frosted glass or ordinary translucent blur.
summary.visualIdentity: Clear glass boundaries with plausible refraction, edge highlights and limited dispersion, so a recognizable background stays visible through the form. Droplets, lenses or flexible panels deform while refraction stays continuous with that deformation.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit source suggestions: hero optical moments where refraction is the feature, and device or feature launches that emphasize clarity or optics. Abstract brand loops and fluid UI concept films are suggested when paired with droplet choreography. A WebGL hero with a static fallback is described for that pairing; broader suitability is inferred.
summary.limitations: Avoid frosted blur passed off as liquid glass, chaotic splashing without a baked simulation, text behind refracting regions, overlapping lenses and rainbow-heavy dispersion. Keep one glass element per product shot. Source review covered only one frame per second for seconds 1–8, so motion and audio were not verified. Results are simulated appearance, not validated physics.
summary.palette: Background policy is scene_dependent: choose the field from subject, mood and lighting, and keep it visible through refraction. Illustrative tokens #EDEBE3 background, #293C49 foreground and #91ACB0 accent_1 are not approved colors. Opaque checks give 9.578 for foreground on background and 4.754 for foreground on accent_1. Gradients are disabled, and scope is new presentation elements only. No task-approved exact colors are specified, so recheck contrast on translucent panels and composited frames.
summary.motionAndInteraction: No fixed motion is mandated; the style requires animated droplets, lenses or panels with deformation-refraction continuity. Candidate catalog references are card stacking (motion-008), pointer tilt (011), chaptered handoff (012), swipe carousel (013), orb deformation (014), storytelling (015), camera orbit (021, which needs real 3D depth) and punctuation zoom (038, a refractive lens only when scene assets support it). Choose none if unsupported. Video runs on composition time; pointer input is optional for interactive delivery.
summary.audio: Unspecified by this style. Audio is only a suggested direction: no genre, tempo, instrument, voice or mandatory layer is assigned. Honor task-provided audio first. Silence is valid. Restrained accents may suit meaningful refractive or transition moments. No source audio was reviewed, and motion references do not require sound.
summary.assetRequirements: No uploads are mandatory. Task copy, fonts and background imagery must load before rendering, and refraction needs a recognizable background or pattern to distort. Punctuation zoom requires inspected glyph or mark geometry. Galleries need accurate image dimensions and fallback links. Audio is used only when authorized. Missing assets must be reported, not invented. Subject, duration, aspect ratio, resolution, frame rate and output directory are unspecified.
summary.combinations: Source-suggested style-114 pairs droplet merge and split choreography with the optics, so refraction follows the deformation; keep dispersion minimal and text outside refracting regions. Source-suggested style-096 pairs product pacing and restrained typography, with one glass element per shot. Both pairings avoid frosted blur. Other combinations are unspecified.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the primary pipeline for assembly, validation and export; Remotion is a fallback only with a recorded reason. Three.js MeshPhysicalMaterial (transmission, ior, roughness) renders the glass, and an offscreen render target supplies the background without feedback loops. GSAP provides the paused timeline. chroma-js can validate contrast, and a labeled SVG displacement approximation is an alternative. Verify seeks and decoded frames.
